Telstra, Optus and Vodafone after a death: keep or cancel the mobile number? (Australia)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 19 Oct 2026

Telstra, Optus and Vodafone all let an authorised person, such as the executor or next of kin, cancel a deceased customer's services or transfer the mobile number into their own name. All three also offer a copy of the voicemail greeting (Vodafone: where available). Ask for it before you cancel or transfer, and consider keeping the number until the person's accounts are sorted.

Key facts

  • Telstra, Optus and Vodafone: cancel or transfer
  • Voicemail greeting copy available on request
  • Transfers: credit check (Optus, Vodafone)
  • Response within 10 business days

What are the steps?

  1. Check you can act. Telstra, Optus and Vodafone accept the executor, administrator or trustee, the lawyer handling the will, next of kin, or an authorised representative on the account. Optus and Vodafone also accept a power of attorney.
  2. Gather documents. Telstra and Vodafone ask for the will or a grant of representation (probate or letters of administration); next of kin may show a birth certificate instead. Administrators show the letters of administration.
  3. List each service (mobile, home internet, email) and decide whether to cancel or transfer it.
  4. Ask for a copy of the voicemail greeting first. Telstra warns it may already be deleted once a transfer or closure has been requested.
  5. Notify the telco. Telstra and Vodafone accept notifications through the Australian Death Notification Service. Directly: Telstra online form, email, post, store or 1800 775 932; Optus Bereavement Care form by email or post; Vodafone on 1555 or 1300 650 410.
  6. Transferring the number? Expect a credit check. Optus asks for at least 100 points of ID and Vodafone says you'll need to meet its credit requirements.
  7. Keep the deceased's Telstra email? Telstra says you need to transfer it to a new account using its Bereavement Support form.
  8. Telstra sends the final bill in the name of 'The Estate of the deceased' to the address the notifier nominates.

Frequently asked questions

Can I keep my late partner's mobile number?

Usually, by transferring it into your name. Telstra, Optus and Vodafone all offer transfers through their bereavement processes. Optus and Vodafone say a credit check or their credit requirements apply.

Can I get a copy of their voicemail greeting?

Yes. Telstra, Optus and Vodafone all offer a digital copy (Vodafone says where available). Ask before you cancel or transfer: Telstra says the greeting may already be deleted after a transfer or closure request, and Optus says custom greetings reset on transfer.

Why not cancel the number straight away?

Many banks, email providers and government services send sign-in or recovery codes by SMS. Keeping the number while accounts are closed through official processes can make that admin easier. Check with the executor before using codes to get into any account.

Does the Australian Death Notification Service notify Telstra and Vodafone?

Yes. Telstra and Vodafone both accept ADNS notifications and say they'll contact you within 10 business days. Optus's bereavement form is returned by email or post.

How long does it take?

Telstra and Optus say their specialist team will contact you within 10 business days, and Vodafone says the same for ADNS notifications. None publishes a fixed completion time.

Who can close a deceased person's phone account?

The executor, administrator or trustee, the lawyer handling the will, next of kin, or an authorised representative on the account. Optus and Vodafone also accept a power of attorney.
